7840.t: Unknown. There are at least two possibilities: # Derived from Proto-Indo-European, through augmented *ḱsendʰ-, from root *ḱas- (“white, blond, grey”).

7835.t: From νέω (néō). The dental enlargement in this term is comparable to other Greek terms such as κνήθω (knḗthō).

7836.t: Borrowed from Semitic. Compare Hebrew נֶתֶר (néṯer, “washing soda”), all ultimately from Egyptian nṯrj: R9

7872.t: Reduplicated nursery word; compare πάππας (páppas, “daddy, papa”).

7802.t: Possibly from Proto-Indo-European *nes- (“to join with, to conceal oneself”), but Beekes considers this uncertain. See νέομαι (néomai, “to go or come back”).

7801.t: Borrowed from Biblical Hebrew נָזִיר (nāzîr, “Nazarite”), perhaps from נִזַּר (nizzar, “separate; consecrate oneself”).

7800.t: Has been connected with Old English næsc (“soft leather; deer skin”) but Beekes suggests a Pre-Greek origin.

7876.t: The formation is like λέπυρον (lépuron), but without a certain explanation. It has been connected to Latin putus (“pure”), Sanskrit पूत (pūtá, “cleansed”) and Proto-Germanic *faujaną (“to sift”), but this is highly unlikely.

7865.t: Unexplained. A basis *ὀδϝός (*odwós) enables connection with οὖδας (oûdas, “ground, soil”), but only if one accepts that this is a generalized Ionic form.

7831.t: From the root of νέμω (némō), from Proto-Indo-European *nem-.

7863.t: Explanation debated. Because of the comparable formation in υἱωνός (huiōnós, “grandson”) from υἱός (huiós, “son”), it is probably best derived from a nominal basis.

7813.t: From νήχω (nḗkhō, “to swim”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)neh₂- (“to flow, to swim”), + -τός (-tós).

7854.t: From οἰκεῖος (oikeîos, “familial, related; familiar, intimate”) + -της (-tēs, abstract noun suffix).
